standard.title: Emotional self-management
standard.description: analyse factors that influence emotional responses and devise strategies to self-manage emotions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have applied strategies to manage emotions and analysed how emotional responses influence interactions (Y5-6). They can apply management strategies and describe their effects on interactions, but have not yet been expected to analyse the range of factors that drive emotional responses.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students analyse factors that influence emotional responses and devise strategies to self-manage emotions.

nodes.label: Identifying factors that influence emotional responses
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify personal, social and cultural factors that influence how individuals respond emotionally to situations, with examples of each factor type.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one factor (personal, social or cultural) that influences emotional responses and give a specific example of how it operates.
nodes.typical_width: Identify personal, social and cultural factors across a range of situations; describe how each factor type can intensify, moderate or shape the nature of emotional responses; examine how context interacts with these factors.
wider: Investigate how cultural backgrounds shape emotional expression and management norms, examining how different cultural expectations create different 'rules' for emotional response in the same situation

Explore how social media and digital environments create distinctive emotional pressures for young people, identifying what factors make online emotional responses particularly intense or difficult to manage
nodes.hinge_reason: Strategy devising requires students to have identified the specific factors their strategies need to address — generic strategies not connected to specific influences are not responsive to the descriptor's demand for analysis-driven devising.

response_modes.reason: Build a systematic factor identification framework (personal/social/cultural) and model applying it to a specific situation. Students should be able to use the framework independently before they attempt strategy devising.

success_criteria: Identifies at least one personal, social or cultural factor that influences emotional responses
Gives a specific example of how that factor operates in a situation

nodes.label: Analysing emotional responses in context
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can analyse how specific factors produce specific emotional responses in given situations and evaluate the potential impact of those responses on others.
nodes.minimum_width: Analyse one situation where specific factors produced an emotional response and describe one potential impact of that response on others.
nodes.typical_width: Analyse emotional responses across multiple situations; practise perspective-taking and empathy to understand how different people experience the same situation differently; recognise and interpret responses to stressful situations.
wider: Explore different viewpoints and practise empathy by considering alternative ways to respond in a variety of situations, examining how the same situation produces different emotional responses for different people based on their personal, social or cultural factors
Analyse emotional responses to stressful situations encountered specifically in digital and online environments, examining how these differ from face-to-face responses and why

response_modes.reason: Emotional analysis is enriched by perspective diversity — encountering how the same situation produces different responses for different people (due to different personal, social, cultural factors) deepens analytical understanding.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Perspective-taking across cultural and social contexts builds genuine empathy and social awareness — students who engage with diverse emotional experiences develop richer emotional intelligence than those who only analyse their own responses.
success_criteria: Analyses at least one factor that produced an emotional response in a specific situation
Identifies at least one potential impact of that emotional response on others

nodes.label: Devising self-management strategies
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can devise strategies to self-manage emotional responses that are specifically responsive to identified influencing factors, and evaluate their likely effectiveness.
nodes.minimum_width: Devise at least one strategy for self-managing an emotional response in a specific situation and give a reason why it would be effective.
nodes.typical_width: Devise a range of self-management strategies responsive to different factor types and situations; evaluate which strategies are most appropriate for specific emotional contexts; ensure proposed strategies prevent negative impact on others.
wider: Recognise and interpret emotional responses to stressful situations and devise strategies that ensure those responses don't negatively impact others, practising strategies in simulated or role-play contexts
Design a personal emotional self-management toolkit that includes strategies for both in-person and digital/online contexts, with justification for each strategy's relevance

response_modes.reason: Devising strategies integrates factor analysis, emotional understanding and practical planning — the strategies produced should be visibly connected to the analysis completed in prior nodes, not generated independently.

success_criteria: Devises at least one strategy for self-managing an emotional response in a specific situation
Explains why the strategy addresses the factors influencing that response
Considers how the strategy prevents or limits negative impact on others
